title: Selfhosting FMHY
description: This guide will help you set up and run your own instance of FMHY locally.

blocks.markdown: Do note that you **must** differentiate your instance from the official site (fmhy.net) to avoid confusion. Steps to do so are given in step 4.
This guide will help you set up and run your own instance of FMHY locally.
To run a local instance, you will need to install [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) and [Docker Compose](https://docs.docker.com/compose/install/).
After installing both, run the following commands:

blocks.code:
git clone https://github.com/fmhy/edit.git
cd edit
sudo docker compose up --build

blocks.markdown: It might take a few minutes to build the image and start the container, running at port 4173.
You can use [nix](https://nixos.org/) to set up a development environment, we have a [flake](https://nixos.wiki/wiki/Flakes) that setups `nodejs` and `pnpm`.

items.markdown: Fork the repository and clone it to your local machine with `git clone https://github.com/fmhy/edit.git`.
Run `nix flake update` to update the flake lock file.
Run `nix develop` to enter the development environment.
Exit the development environment by running `exit`.

blocks.markdown: You will need to install the following:
To run the project in development mode:

blocks.code:
# Start the documentation site in dev mode
pnpm docs:dev

# Start the API in dev mode (if needed)
pnpm api:dev

blocks.markdown: The development server will start at `http://localhost:5173` by default.
To build the project for production:

blocks.code:
# Build the documentation site
pnpm docs:build

# Build the API (if needed) using the Node.js preset
NITRO_PRESET=node pnpm api:build

blocks.markdown: To preview the production build locally:

blocks.code:
# Preview the documentation site
pnpm docs:preview

# Preview the API (if needed)
pnpm api:preview

blocks.markdown: See the [VitePress deployment guide](https://vitepress.dev/guide/deploy) for more info.
If you want to deploy the API component (feedback system), you'll need to set up Cloudflare Workers and KV storage.
Update `wrangler.toml` with your Cloudflare account information:

items.markdown: Get your account ID from the Cloudflare dashboard (found in the right sidebar)
Replace the `account_id` value in `wrangler.toml` with your account ID
If you're using a custom domain, keep `workers_dev = false` and update the `routes` section
If you're deploying to `*.workers.dev`, set `workers_dev = true` and remove the `routes` section

blocks.markdown: Create a KV namespace for data storage:
This command will return a namespace ID. Copy this ID and replace the `id` value in the `[[kv_namespaces]]` section of `wrangler.toml` (line 14).
**Note:** If you want to deploy without running Wrangler locally (e.g., in CI/CD), you'll need to:

items.markdown: Create the KV namespace manually in the Cloudflare dashboard
Update both the `account_id` and `id` values in `wrangler.toml` in your fork

blocks.code:
# Build the API
pnpm api:build

# Deploy to Cloudflare Workers
pnpm api:deploy

blocks.markdown: The API will be deployed to your configured domain or `*.workers.dev` subdomain.

The rate limiter binding requires setup through the Cloudflare dashboard. You can skip this for basic deployments or configure it later through the Workers dashboard under the "Rate limiting" section.
These variables control what gets included when building the documentation site:

items.markdown: `FMHY_BUILD_API` - Enable API component for feedback system

blocks.markdown: These variables are used by the deployed Cloudflare Worker API:

items.markdown: `WEBHOOK_URL` - Discord webhook URL for posting feedback messages (required for API feedback functionality)
If you encounter Node.js version issues, ensure you're using Node.js 21+
For pnpm-related issues, ensure you're using pnpm 9+
If you encounter build issues, try clearing cache:

children.code:
# Linux
rm -rf docs/.vitepress/cache

# PowerShell
rm -r -fo docs/.vitepress/cache

blocks.markdown: You should be able to use any reverse proxy with this vitepress website, but find a reasonable config for an nginx server [in the repo here](https://github.com/fmhy/edit/blob/main/.github/assets/nginx.conf)
